processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Raw materials with high purity (>99.9 %) melted using a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere to produce the Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu ingot from which this sample derives.
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm; plates then cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples by electrical discharge machining.

Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere followed by oil quenching; produces the single-phase α (BCC) soft solid-solution state that is the parent of all subsequent aging treatments.

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase α (Body-centered cubic, BCC) solid solution; coarse-grained microstructure in the solution-treated (1100 °C/10 min + oil quenched) state.

phases_present.grain_size: very coarse grains, tens to hundreds of µm

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: a few very large grains, tens to hundreds of µm (coarse-grained)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness measured with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s using an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester; each sample repeatedly tested 5 times and hardness given by the average.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N for 15 s; 5 repeated measurements averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the hardness of the solution-treated 15Al alloy (solid-solution baseline).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: GeminiSEM 300 SEM; scanning step size 1.5 μm for low magnification and 0.05 μm for high magnification
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished samples (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol)
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the constituent phases and grain structure of the solution-treated 15Al alloy.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Solution-treated 15Al consists of a single α (BCC) phase (phase map uniformly red); IPF map shows a few very coarse grains (tens to hundreds of µm).

characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the density of the 15Al alloy.

unmapped_findings: The solution-treated Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels of all three Al contents (15Al, 17Al, 19Al) are single-phase α (BCC) with no resolvable γ (FCC); the α grain structure is markedly refined as Al increases from 15 to 19 at.% (figure_003, b0040).

The hardness of the solution-treated alloys increased with rising Al content (15Al = 253.4 HV, 17Al = 259.8 HV, 19Al = 263.8 HV), attributed to the solid-solution strengthening effect (b0036, Tables 2-4).

The 15Al solution-treated solid-solution state is explicitly identified as the soft parent state of all subsequent aging treatments; its aliases include 'soft state' and 'ST' (b0017, process definition).

The elastic modulus of 164 GPa for the 15Al alloy (measured through compressive stress-strain curves) is reported in connection with the KIC calculation of the hardest (aged) sample (b0023), so it cannot be unambiguously attributed to the solution-treated state and is therefore not entered as this sample's youngs_modulus.

Sample preparation for Vickers/EBSD/SEM/XRD was electrolytic polishing with 10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol; TEM foils were mechanically ground to ~90 µm, punched to 3 mm discs and ion thinned (b0017).
